findings.title: Legacy SQL-command entry point is not explicitly disabled
findings.body: UnmarshalSQLCommand still constructs a SQLCommand through NewSQLCommand without any disabled/feature check. The newer ExpressionQueryReader is explicitly described as not yet replacing the existing transform.go query path, so this legacy path remains reachable. It is currently blocked only incidentally because sql.TablesList calls the new stub DB and fails, which is then reported as a generic invalid-SQL BadRequest. If the stub DB is later implemented or replaced, this entry point would re-enable SQL execution without passing through the reader's kill-switch and could re-expose the DuckDB RCE/LFI surface. Reject SQL explicitly in UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand, or in the service pipeline builder, with the same disabled/not-implemented error used by the reader.

findings.title: No tests lock in that SQL expressions stay disabled
findings.body: The change adds an early rejection for QueryTypeSQL and stubs out the SQL DB in pkg/expr/sql/db.go, but no test files are changed. There is therefore no regression test proving a SQL expression is rejected even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled, and no updated/skipped coverage for the existing SQL parser/command tests whose TablesList/QueryFramesInto calls now always return 'not implemented'. Add tests for the disabled behavior on both query-parsing entry points and update or explicitly skip the now-obsolete DuckDB-backed SQL tests so CI demonstrates the CVE fix rather than merely failing or silently losing coverage.
